before.label: Memory coalescing and bank conflicts
before.definition: Access patterns that merge a warp's loads into few memory transactions, or that serialize on shared-memory banks.

fields.label: Memory coalescing
fields.definition: Combining memory requests from threads in a warp into fewer global-memory transactions, reducing wasted memory traffic.

changes.rationale: Global-memory transaction coalescing and shared-memory bank serialization are distinct mechanisms; preserve the old identity for its named mechanism.

sources.supports: Global-memory transaction coalescing and shared-memory bank serialization are distinct mechanisms; preserve the old identity for its named mechanism.

impact.classification: Retain the existing identity for coalescing; add bank conflicts as a distinct mechanism in the same subject.
impact.assignments: Existing assignments remain on the old identity pending item-level review; do not automatically assign bank conflicts.
impact.relationships: Keep coalescing layout and thread links; qualify its bandwidth edge and give bank conflicts its own bandwidth edge.

fields.label: Shared-memory bank conflict
fields.definition: Serialization of a shared-memory request when threads access different addresses in the same bank, reducing effective shared-memory bandwidth.

changes.rationale: A bank conflict is a separate failure of parallel shared-memory access, not another name for global-memory coalescing.

sources.supports: A bank conflict is a separate failure of parallel shared-memory access, not another name for global-memory coalescing.

impact.classification: Retain the existing identity for coalescing; add bank conflicts as a distinct mechanism in the same subject.
impact.assignments: Existing assignments remain on the old identity pending item-level review; do not automatically assign bank conflicts.
impact.relationships: Keep coalescing layout and thread links; qualify its bandwidth edge and give bank conflicts its own bandwidth edge.

before.conditions: Uncoalesced or bank-conflicted accesses waste transactions, so effective bandwidth falls below peak.

fields.conditions: For global-memory accesses by a warp, coalescing reduces wasted transactions; achieved bandwidth also depends on the workload and hardware.

changes.rationale: Restrict this relationship to global-memory coalescing; bank conflicts now have a separate record.

sources.supports: Restrict this relationship to global-memory coalescing; bank conflicts now have a separate record.

fields.conditions: Different addresses in the same shared-memory bank require serialized requests; same-address broadcast is excluded.

changes.rationale: Serialized bank-conflicting requests lower effective bandwidth; the broadcast exception limits this assertion.

sources.supports: Serialized bank-conflicting requests lower effective bandwidth; the broadcast exception limits this assertion.

impact.classification: Retain the existing identity for coalescing; add bank conflicts as a distinct mechanism in the same subject.
impact.assignments: Existing assignments remain on the old identity pending item-level review; do not automatically assign bank conflicts.
impact.relationships: Keep coalescing layout and thread links; qualify its bandwidth edge and give bank conflicts its own bandwidth edge.

before.label: Tracing and JIT capture
before.definition: Recording operations executed on example inputs to build a graph compiled just in time, with guards or retracing when shapes or control flow change.

fields.label: Graph tracing
fields.definition: Recording supported operations during a program execution with concrete or abstract inputs to construct an intermediate graph for transformation, compilation, or export.

changes.rationale: Tracing constructs an intermediate representation; JIT compilation is a later use and is not an equivalent name.

sources.supports: Tracing constructs an intermediate representation; JIT compilation is a later use and is not an equivalent name.

impact.classification: Preserve the historical identity for graph tracing; compilation remains an existing separate concept.
impact.assignments: Existing tags need review only when they intended compilation timing rather than graph capture.
impact.relationships: Recheck all four incident edges; qualify tracing-dependent transformations and export, and remove the eager-execution dependency.

before.conditions: Traced shapes and control flow remain valid for later inputs or guards trigger recompilation.

fields.conditions: A compiler accepts the traced intermediate graph and its assumptions about inputs and control flow hold.

changes.rationale: A traced graph can be compiled; tracing itself does not determine whether compilation occurs ahead of time or at run time.

sources.supports: A traced graph can be compiled; tracing itself does not determine whether compilation occurs ahead of time or at run time.

before.conditions: Transformations are applied to a traced intermediate representation, so Python side effects and data-dependent control flow are not captured.

fields.conditions: For transformations implemented over a traced intermediate representation, such as JAX transformations; this is not a requirement for every transformation implementation.

changes.rationale: Qualify the implementation dependency rather than treating tracing as necessary for all function transformations.

sources.supports: Qualify the implementation dependency rather than treating tracing as necessary for all function transformations.

before.conditions: The program is traced or captured on example inputs; untraced control flow is lost.

fields.conditions: In export workflows that obtain a graph by tracing, such as JAX export; tracing and lowering may precede execution on another machine.

changes.rationale: JAX explicitly separates tracing and lowering from later execution; the edge denotes a supported export workflow, not a universal JIT requirement.

sources.supports: JAX explicitly separates tracing and lowering from later execution; the edge denotes a supported export workflow, not a universal JIT requirement.

before.conditions: When operations run on example inputs are recorded into a graph for later compilation, with guards or retracing when shapes or control flow change.

changes.rationale: JAX uses tracer objects with abstract values; graph tracing does not generally require eager tensor execution. Remove the stronger dependency.

before.label: Tolerable risk and ALARP
before.definition: The criteria that decide which identified hazards need controls and when residual risk is acceptable, ranking hazards by severity and likelihood and requiring reduction until further reduction is grossly disproportionate to its benefit.

fields.label: Risk acceptance criteria
fields.definition: Criteria used to judge whether residual risk is acceptable or tolerable in a stated application and whether additional risk reduction is required.

changes.rationale: Tolerability criteria and ALARP risk-reduction reasoning are related but distinct. Retain the criteria identity; do not universalize one regulatory framework.

sources.supports: Tolerability criteria and ALARP risk-reduction reasoning are related but distinct. Retain the criteria identity; do not universalize one regulatory framework.

impact.classification: Retain the existing identity for criteria used by hazard analysis and safety cases; ALARP is not an equivalent label.
impact.assignments: Review tags that specifically intended ALARP; the broader criteria concept remains available.
impact.relationships: Retain hazard-analysis and safety-case criteria links; remove the unsupported direct integrity-level determination.

changes.rationale: A generic risk-acceptance criterion does not itself set an automotive integrity level; the existing edge conflates a domain risk-classification procedure with criteria.
